$comment: Failure scenarios for the Web Bot Auth profile, as data. A harness signs each request, directory, and response scenario at run time, applies after_signing, and grades the verifier on expected: a pass, or a refusal by its status and rule (refusals.json). created and expires are offsets in seconds from the harness clock; a null parameter is omitted; a nonce object asks for that many random bytes in that encoding. verifier is the verifier's own authority, which a request scenario's authority replaces. tier "wba": the reference libraries with no profile rules already give the expected outcome. tier "profile": the bare libraries give the opposite outcome and only the profile's rules give the expected one; a WBA MUST the library does not enforce stays "profile" until it does. Each target_uris case is a GET to url, which each side signs and the other verifies; wire is its @target-uri. See README.md.

request_scenarios.name: Baseline
request_scenarios.basis: Profile rules
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Body changed after signing
request_scenarios.basis: Content-Digest matches the body: RFC 9530; WBA section 5.2
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Covered header changed after signing
request_scenarios.basis: RFC 9421 section 3.2
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Expired
request_scenarios.basis: RFC 9421 section 3.2.1
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: created 120 seconds in the future
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: 60 seconds of clock skew
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: created 30 seconds in the future
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: 60 seconds of clock skew; the library allows none by default
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Lifetime of 3600 seconds
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: expires at most 300 seconds after created
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Nonce of 32 bytes
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: 64-byte nonce; validateNonce
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Nonce in canonical padded base64
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: unpadded base64url or canonical padded base64
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Nonce in padded base64url
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: unpadded base64url or canonical padded base64
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: No alg parameter
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: alg required
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: alg other than ed25519
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: alg is ed25519 and matches the key; RFC 9421 section 3.2
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: GET covering only @authority and the Signature-Agent member
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: cover @method, @target-uri, and @authority; WBA section 5.2 needs one of @authority or @target-uri
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Body without content-digest covered
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: a request with a body covers content-type and content-digest; WBA section 5.2
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Body without content-type covered
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: a request with a body covers content-type and content-digest
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: tag other than web-bot-auth
request_scenarios.basis: WBA section 5.2: tag MUST be web-bot-auth
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Components in another order
request_scenarios.basis: RFC 9421: the order is the signer's
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: No nonce
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: a nonce on every signed request; WBA leaves it to deployment policy
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: GET with the profile's components
request_scenarios.basis: Profile rules; a request without a body covers no content-digest
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Bare-string Signature-Agent
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: dictionary form only, so the field does not parse; WBA section 5.2.1 lets a verifier accept the bare string
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: http:// key URL
request_scenarios.basis: WBA section 5.2.1: the scheme MUST be https; the library accepts http (cloudflare/web-bot-auth#162)
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: http:// origin
request_scenarios.basis: WBA section 5.2.1: the scheme MUST be https
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Path other than the well-known path
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; the library does not check it
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Well-known path with a trailing /
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no trailing /
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Well-known path in another case
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; the path is compared as a string
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Origin with a trailing /
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no trailing /
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Uppercase host
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; a lowercase host
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Explicit :443
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no port
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Other port
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no port
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Query
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no query
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Fragment
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no fragment
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Userinfo
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no userinfo
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Origin with a query
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: the value is exactly https://<host>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory or https://<host>, compared without normalizing; no query
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Member with type=jwks_uri
request_scenarios.basis: WBA -01 section 5.2.1: a verifier MUST ignore a member that carries parameters
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Origin member with type=directory as a Token
request_scenarios.basis: WBA -01 section 5.2.1: members MUST NOT carry parameters, and a verifier MUST ignore one that does
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Key URL member with type="directory" as a String
request_scenarios.basis: WBA -01 section 5.2.1: members MUST NOT carry parameters, and a verifier MUST ignore one that does
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Bare origin, the draft -00 form
request_scenarios.basis: WBA -00 section 5.5: a directory member is an origin; the verifier fetches the same well-known URL
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Signature-Agent member keyed differently from the label
request_scenarios.basis: WBA section 5.2.1: the member keyed to the label; the library does not check it
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Two Signature-Agent members, one signature
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: exactly one Signature-Agent member
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Label other than sig1
request_scenarios.basis: RFC 9421: the signer chooses the label
request_scenarios.label: wba

request_scenarios.name: Second signature with tag cdn-edge
request_scenarios.basis: Profile: Signature-Input members with other tags are not read; the library requires a label when a request carries two signatures
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Second member with tag cdn-edge whose Signature value is a token
request_scenarios.basis: RFC 9421 section 4.2: every Signature member value is a Byte Sequence, so the field is malformed whatever the member's tag
request_scenarios.label: sig1

request_scenarios.name: Signed for seller.example.com, verified by seller-b.example.com
request_scenarios.basis: OpenProposal § 2.8.4 step 5: the signed @authority is the verifier's own configured authority, never the Host it was sent
request_scenarios.label: sig1

directory_scenarios.name: Body changed after signing
directory_scenarios.basis: WBA Appendix B.1: the verifier MUST validate Content-Digest; the library does not compare it with the body

directory_scenarios.name: Unsigned
directory_scenarios.basis: Profile: every Ed25519 key signs (Appendix B.1 recommends it)

directory_scenarios.name: Signature created in the future
directory_scenarios.basis: WBA Appendix B.1: reject a future created; the profile allows the same 60 s skew as for requests

directory_scenarios.name: Extra P-256 key that does not sign
directory_scenarios.basis: Profile: ignore keys the profile does not use (RFC 7517 section 5)

directory_scenarios.name: Media type application/json
directory_scenarios.basis: WBA section 5.5.1: the well-known directory MUST be served with application/http-message-signatures-directory+json

directory_scenarios.name: Signature expired one second ago
directory_scenarios.basis: Profile: the clock skew applies to created only; a directory verifies until its expires

directory_scenarios.name: Signature that expires now
directory_scenarios.basis: Profile: a directory verifies until its expires, that second included

response_scenarios.name: Baseline, bound to the signed request
response_scenarios.label: sig1

response_scenarios.name: Signed request, response not bound to it
response_scenarios.basis: Profile: a response to a signed request covers "signature";req;key=<request label>
response_scenarios.label: sig1

response_scenarios.name: Bound to another request
response_scenarios.basis: RFC 9421 section 2.4: the request's signature is covered
response_scenarios.label: sig1

response_scenarios.name: Lifetime of 3600 seconds
response_scenarios.basis: Profile: expires at most 300 seconds after created
response_scenarios.label: sig1

response_scenarios.name: Unsigned request, response without a binding
response_scenarios.basis: Profile: the binding applies when the request carried a signature
response_scenarios.label: sig1

response_scenarios.name: Response signed with tag other than web-bot-auth
response_scenarios.label: sig1

target_uris.basis: Profile: @target-uri is the URL as it travels on the wire (RFC 3986 § 6.2.2)
